questions.question: The metal whose oxide can be reduced by common reducing agent:
questions.solution: (a) Copper. Oxides of metals low in the activity series (like CuO) are reduced by C, CO or H2; oxides of Na, K, Al need electrolytic reduction.

questions.question: The molecular formula that represents saturated hydrocarbon is:
questions.solution: (b) C5H12. Saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes) follow CnH2n+2; C5H12 fits.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): The tendency of losing electrons increases down the Group.
Reason (R): The most reactive metal is placed on the top of Group 1.

options.a: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true.

questions.solution: (c) A is true but R is false. Atomic size increases down the group so electrons are lost more easily (A true); the most reactive metal is at the bottom of Group 1, not the top (R false).

questions.question: Aqueous lead (II) nitrate can be distinguished from aqueous zinc nitrate by adding any of the following solutions in excess except:
questions.solution: (d) sodium hydroxide solution.. Both Pb(OH)2 and Zn(OH)2 are white precipitates that dissolve in excess NaOH, so NaOH cannot distinguish them; KCl, Na2SO4 and dil. H2SO4 give a white precipitate (PbCl2 / PbSO4) only with lead nitrate.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question: Identify from the following the metal oxide which can react with an acid as well as an alkali.
questions.solution: (d) Aluminium oxide. Al2O3 is amphoteric.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.question:
Four reactions are shown below in the diagram: 1. calcium carbonate heated in a dish over a burner; 2. zinc added to dilute hydrochloric acid in a flask; 3. ethanol burning in a spirit lamp; 4. magnesium carbonate added to dilute sulphuric acid in a flask.
Which reactions produce water?
questions.solution: (c) 3 and 4. Burning ethanol gives CO2 + H2O; MgCO3 + H2SO4 -> MgSO4 + H2O + CO2. Heating CaCO3 gives CaO + CO2 and Zn + HCl gives ZnCl2 + H2 - no water.

questions.question:
The structures of four hydrocarbons are shown below. How many isomers of butene are shown in the structures?
Structure 1: CH3-CH(CH3)-CH3 (drawn as H3C-C(H)(CH3)-CH3)
Structure 2: CH3-C(=CH2)-CH3 (C=CH2 with two CH3 groups)
Structure 3: CH3-CH2-CH=CH2
Structure 4: H3C-C(CH3)=CH2
questions.solution: (b) 2. Structure 1 is 2-methylpropane (C4H10, an alkane). Structures 2 and 4 are the same compound, 2-methylpropene, and structure 3 is but-1-ene. So two different isomers of butene (C4H8) are shown. (If the key counts drawings with formula C4H8, it would give 3.)

questions.question: Nitrogen gas can be obtained by heating:
questions.solution: (b) ammonium nitrite. NH4NO2 -> N2 + 2H2O on heating; ammonium nitrate gives N2O.

questions.topic: Electrolysis of CuSO4 with copper electrodes
concepts: Electrolysis of CuSO4 with copper electrodes
questions.question: Aqueous copper (II) sulphate is electrolysed using copper electrodes. Which statement about the electrolysis is not correct?

options.a: An oxidation reaction occurs at the positive electrode.
options.b: The current is carried through the electrolyte by ions
options.d: The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.

questions.solution: (d) The number of copper (II) ions in the electrolyte decreases.. The copper anode dissolves (Cu -> Cu2+ + 2e-) at the same rate as Cu2+ is deposited at the cathode, so the Cu2+ concentration stays constant.

questions.question: The electronic configuration of X is 2,8,6. It gains 'Y' electrons into its valence shell to attain the nearest noble gas electronic configuration and gets converted to an ion Z. X, Y and Z, respectively are:
questions.solution: (d) Sulphur, two, electronegative. 2,8,6 is sulphur (Z = 16); it gains 2 electrons to form S2- (argon configuration), an electronegative ion.

questions.question: The formation of ethane from ethene is a:
questions.solution: (c) hydrogenation reaction. C2H4 + H2 -(Ni, 300 C)-> C2H6 is hydrogenation (which is itself an addition reaction, so (d) is also acceptable).

questions.topic: Products at anode in electrolysis of chlorides
concepts: Products at anode in electrolysis of chlorides
questions.question: Three aqueous solutions, L, M and N, are electrolysed using inert electrodes. L is concentrated hydrochloric acid. M is concentrated aqueous sodium chloride. N is dilute aqueous sodium chloride. Which solutions produce a pale yellow-green gas at the anode?
questions.solution: (a) L and M. Concentrated chloride solutions discharge Cl- (chlorine at anode); dilute NaCl discharges OH- giving oxygen.

questions.question:
Assertion (A): Carboxylic acid reacts with alcohol in the presence of concentrated H2SO4 to produce a fruity smell.
Reason (R): It is due to the formation of alcohol.

options.a: Both A and R are individually true and R is the correct explanation of A
options.b: Both A and R are individually true but R is not the correct explanation of A
options.c: A is true but R is false
options.d: A is false but R is true.

questions.solution: (c) A is true but R is false. The fruity smell is due to the ester formed (esterification), not alcohol.

questions.question: Ammonia is produced industrially from nitrogen and hydrogen: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3. The forward reaction is exothermic. Which change would not alter the yield of ammonia?

options.d: Removing some ammonia during the reaction.

questions.solution: (a) Adding a catalyst. A catalyst only increases the rate at which equilibrium is reached; it does not shift the equilibrium/yield.

questions.question:
Which of the following would occupy 22.4 L at S.T.P.?
(i) 32 g of oxygen
(ii) 2 moles of hydrogen gas
(iii) 6.023 x 10^23 molecules of ammonia
questions.solution: (b) (i) and (iii). 32 g O2 = 1 mol and 6.023 x 10^23 molecules = 1 mol, each occupying 22.4 L; 2 mol H2 occupies 44.8 L.

questions.question:
(a) Draw the structural diagram for the following compounds:
(a) Propanoic acid  (b) Pentan-2-ol  (c) 2,2-dibromobutane
(b) Give the IUPAC name of the following organic compounds:
(A) H-C(H)(H)-C(=O)-H  [a CH3 group attached to a CHO group]
(B) H2C=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3  [four-carbon chain with a C=C between C1 and C2 and a CH3 branch on C3]
questions.solution:
(a) (a) Propanoic acid: CH3-CH2-COOH, drawn H3C-CH2-C(=O)-O-H with all bonds shown.
(b) Pentan-2-ol: CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-CH3, -OH on the second carbon of a five-carbon chain.
(c) 2,2-dibromobutane: CH3-CBr2-CH2-CH3, both Br atoms on carbon 2.
(b) (A) Ethanal (CH3CHO)
(B) 3-methylbut-1-ene

questions.question:
Match the following column A with column B:
Column A: 1. Neon; 2. Methane; 3. Ostwald's process; 4. Esterification; 5. Ammonia gas in water
Column B: a) ammonium ion; b) zero electron affinity; c) Non-polar; d) Platinum; e) ethanol
questions.solution: 1-b (Neon: zero electron affinity, stable octet); 2-c (Methane: non-polar covalent molecule); 3-d (Ostwald's process: platinum catalyst); 4-e (Esterification: ethanol reacts with an acid); 5-a (Ammonia in water: NH3 + H2O -> NH4+ + OH-).

questions.question:
The question is related to the gas X. Fill in the blanks:
(a) An aqueous solution of gas X turns red litmus blue, so it must contain ______ (hydrogen / hydroxyl) ions.
(b) When the above solution is added in excess to copper sulphate solution, it turns to ______ (deep blue / pale blue) solution.
(c) Gas X is also a good ______ (oxidizing / reducing) agent, which in excess reacts with a greenish-yellow gas to form dense white fumes of ______ (hydrogen chloride / ammonium chloride).
(d) The gas X ______ (oxidises / reduces) copper oxide to copper.

answer_items.prompt: (d) gas X ______ copper oxide to copper

questions.solution:
X is ammonia.
(a) hydroxyl
(b) deep blue (tetraamminecopper(II) sulphate)
(c) reducing; ammonium chloride (8NH3 + 3Cl2 -> 6NH4Cl + N2)
(d) reduces (2NH3 + 3CuO -> 3Cu + 3H2O + N2)

questions.question:
Identify the following:
(a) Undistilled alcohol containing a large amount of methanol.
(b) A homogeneous mixture of two or more metals or metals and non-metals.
(c) That part of an organic compound which defines the structure and properties of that organic compound is called.
(d) The alloy of lead and tin used in electrical circuits.
(e) The tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms.

answer_items.prompt: Undistilled alcohol with a large amount of methanol
Homogeneous mixture of metals or metals and non-metals
Part of an organic compound defining its properties
Alloy of lead and tin used in electrical circuits
Tendency of an element to form chains of identical atoms

questions.solution:
(a) Spurious alcohol
(b) Alloy
(c) Functional group
(d) Solder
(e) Catenation

questions.question:
The diagram shows an apparatus for the laboratory preparation of hydrogen chloride (round-bottom flask with reactant B at the bottom, thistle funnel A, delivery tube leading into a gas jar where hydrogen chloride gas is collected by upward displacement of air).
(i) Identify A and B.
(ii) Write the equation for the reaction.
(iii) Write the test of the gas produced.
(iv) What does the method of collection tell you about the density of hydrogen chloride gas?
(v) Why is this gas not dried with calcium oxide?
questions.solution:
(i) A = concentrated sulphuric acid (added through the thistle funnel); B = sodium chloride (rock salt).
(ii) NaCl + H2SO4 (conc.) -(below 200 C)-> NaHSO4 + HCl
(iii) A glass rod dipped in ammonia solution held at the mouth of the jar gives dense white fumes of NH4Cl (or: the gas gives a curdy white precipitate with silver nitrate solution).
(iv) It is collected by upward displacement of air, so HCl is heavier (denser) than air.
(v) CaO is basic and reacts with acidic HCl: CaO + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O.

marking_points.point: CaO is basic, reacts with HCl

questions.figure_desc: Lab apparatus for HCl: round-bottom flask with substance B, thistle funnel labelled A, delivery tube into an upright gas jar labelled 'Hydrogen chloride gas'.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: An organic compound X contains carbon, hydrogen and oxygen only. The percentage of carbon and hydrogen are 47.4% and 10.5% respectively. The relative molecular mass of 'X' is 76. Find the empirical and molecular formula of X. (Atomic mass: C = 12, H = 1, O = 16)
questions.solution:
O% = 100 - 47.4 - 10.5 = 42.1%
C: 47.4/12 = 3.95; H: 10.5/1 = 10.5; O: 42.1/16 = 2.63
Divide by 2.63: C 1.5, H 4, O 1 -> multiply by 2: C 3, H 8, O 2
Empirical formula = C3H8O2; EF mass = 36 + 8 + 32 = 76
n = 76/76 = 1, so molecular formula = C3H8O2.

marking_points.point: Moles/relative ratio of C, H, O

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Define the following terms:
(a) Isomerism
(b) Homologous series
questions.solution:
(a) Isomerism: the phenomenon in which compounds have the same molecular formula but different structural formulae (and properties).
(b) Homologous series: a group of organic compounds with the same functional group and general formula, similar chemical properties, in which successive members differ by a CH2 group.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Conductivity of ionic and covalent compounds
concepts: Conductivity of ionic and covalent compounds
questions.question:
Justify the following statements:
(a) Ionic compounds conduct electricity in molten state or aqueous state.
(b) Non-polar covalent compounds do not conduct electricity in aqueous solution.
questions.solution:
(a) In the molten or aqueous state the strong electrostatic forces are overcome and the ions become free to move, so they carry current.
(b) Non-polar covalent compounds consist of molecules and do not ionise in water, so there are no free ions to conduct electricity.

marking_points.point: Ions free to move in molten/aqueous state

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Extraction of zinc from zinc blende
questions.question:
A student was asked to draw the flowchart for the extraction of zinc from zinc blende based on the principles of metallurgy. What he drew is given below. 2 steps out of the 5 were incorrect. Identify and correct them.
Flowchart: Zinc blende (ZnS) (ore) -> (1) Pulverisation -> (2) Leaching (concentration of the ore) -> (3) Calcination (oxidation of the ore) -> (4) Chemical reduction (using coke) -> (5) Refining (by electrolysis) -> Pure zinc
questions.solution:
Incorrect step (2): Leaching is wrong. Zinc blende is a sulphide ore, so it is concentrated by froth flotation.
Incorrect step (3): Calcination is wrong. A sulphide ore is converted to the oxide by roasting (heating in excess air): 2ZnS + 3O2 -> 2ZnO + 2SO2.
Steps 1, 4 (ZnO + C -> Zn + CO) and 5 are correct.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
A student prepared a potassium sulphite solution in the lab and added few drops of barium nitrate solution to it. He observed a white precipitate being formed in the test tube. On addition of dilute hydrochloric acid to the white precipitate and mixing it, he observed that the precipitate disappeared.
(a) Name the white precipitate.
(b) Write a balanced chemical equation for the reaction between dilute hydrochloric acid and the white precipitate.
(c) Name the gas evolved in the above reaction.
questions.solution:
(a) Barium sulphite (BaSO3)
(b) BaSO3 + 2HCl -> BaCl2 + H2O + SO2
(c) Sulphur dioxide (SO2)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.topic: Bond type and formula from electronic configuration
concepts: Bond type and formula from electronic configuration
questions.question:
The following table shows the electronic configuration of the elements W, X, Y, Z. [Note: the table of electronic configurations is not printed in the source paper.]
(a) What type of bond is formed between: (i) W and X  (ii) Y and Z
(c) What is the formula of the compound formed between: (i) W and X  (ii) W and X
questions.solution: The configuration table is missing from the printed paper, so the answer depends on it. Method: a metal (1-3 valence electrons) with a non-metal (5-7 valence electrons) forms an ionic (electrovalent) bond; two non-metals form a covalent bond. Formula: cross the valencies. For example, if W = 2,8,1 (valency 1) and X = 2,7 (valency 1), the bond is ionic and the formula is WX; if Y = 2,4 and Z = 1 (H), the bond is covalent and the formula is YZ4.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question: For construction work the alloy of aluminium i.e. Duralumin is used rather than pure aluminium. Give two valid reasons.
questions.solution:
1. Duralumin is much stronger and harder than pure aluminium (pure Al is soft).
2. It is light and resists corrosion, so it gives strength without adding much weight.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
1 mole of CO2 occupies 24 dm3 at room temperature and pressure. Calculate the following:
(a) The mass of 6 litres of CO2.
(b) The volume occupied by 60 g of CO2. [Atomic weight: C = 12, O = 16]
questions.solution:
Molar mass of CO2 = 44 g.
(a) 6 L = 6/24 = 0.25 mol; mass = 0.25 x 44 = 11 g
(b) 60 g = 60/44 = 1.364 mol; volume = 1.364 x 24 = 32.73 dm3 (about 32.7 L)

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B
questions.question:
Define:
(a) Electrolyte
(b) Catenation
questions.solution:
(a) Electrolyte: a compound which, in the molten state or in aqueous solution, conducts electricity and is decomposed by it (due to free ions).
(b) Catenation: the property of an element (especially carbon) of forming long chains or rings by bonding with atoms of the same element.

questions.choice_note: any 4 of 6 questions in Section B

questions.question:
Name the most appropriate method of preparation of the following salts:
(a) Copper carbonate
(b) Sodium sulphate
(c) Ferric chloride
questions.solution:
(a) Precipitation (double decomposition), e.g. CuSO4 + Na2CO3 -> CuCO3 + Na2SO4
(b) Neutralisation by titration (2NaOH + H2SO4 -> Na2SO4 + 2H2O)
(c) Direct combination (synthesis): 2Fe + 3Cl2 -> 2FeCl3
